title: 面试高频：Bitmap、LMKD、PSI、水位与 ZRAM
key_conclusions: Bitmap interview answers should separate decode peak, cache residency, Native/Graphics attribution, and Android version boundaries.
LMKD answers need kill-time evidence: oom_score_adj, pressure, victim RSS, lmkd reason, and exit/stats signals.
PSI is a stall signal, not just a low-free-memory proxy, and should be tied to reclaim, ZRAM, frames, and lmkd.
Watermark and ZRAM tuning are tradeoffs that require rollback metrics for jank, kills, CPU, and swap latency.
shallow_points: The article provides interview answer templates but does not include real candidate transcripts or scoring rubrics.
It does not attach real meminfo, showmap, lmkd, PSI, vmstat, or zram mm_stat samples.
It does not validate Android 17 Bitmap or lmkd source behavior against a local AOSP checkout.
It does not quantify safe ZRAM or watermark tuning ranges for specific RAM classes.
discovered_connections: Day 76's answer framework works for system memory questions when each answer starts with boundary, bucket, signal, source hook, fix, and validation.
Day 75's version-aware evidence model is necessary for Bitmap attribution, lmkd behavior, ZRAM, and Android 17 diagnostics.
Day 73's observe, attribute, intervene, validate loop becomes the structure for watermark and ZRAM tradeoff answers.
Day 78 should combine Bitmap/LMKD/PSI/watermark/ZRAM answers into a single low-end incident timeline.
suggest_future_topics: Day 78 should focus on a comprehensive low-end memory case with one timestamp-aligned timeline.
A future appendix should include real lmkd, PSI, vmstat, zram, meminfo, and Perfetto snippets.
A future mock interview should score Bitmap and LMKD answers by evidence depth.
A future lab should quantify watermark and ZRAM side effects by RAM class.
knowledge_gaps: Need real diagnostic artifacts to demonstrate Bitmap, lmkd, PSI, watermark, and ZRAM answers.
Need local AOSP validation for Android 17 memory behavior and branch-specific lmkd fields.
Need measured low-end device data for ZRAM size, compression ratio, swap latency, and PSI movement.
Need a scoring rubric that distinguishes generic answers from senior-level system memory reasoning.
